How to choose between laser treatments
Pico vs Diode vs Fractional: Choosing a Laser | The Better Face
A plain-language guide to which laser does what, who each one suits, and the questions to ask any clinic before you book. Written by our clinical team.

Most people arrive having been told a laser will fix their skin, without ever
being told which laser, or why. The category is genuinely confusing, so here is
the short version.

## They are not interchangeable

Lasers are chosen by what they target. Pigment, blood vessels, hair and water
all absorb light differently, and a device tuned for one is close to useless
for another. A clinic offering "laser" as a single service is a clinic to ask
harder questions of.

## The three you will most often be offered

**Pico** targets pigment. Ultra-short pulses shatter it mechanically rather
than burning it, which puts less heat into the skin — the reason it is usually
the safer choice on deeper skin tones.

**Diode** targets the hair follicle. It is a hair-reduction device. It will not
do anything meaningful for pigmentation.

**Fractional resurfacing** targets water in the tissue to drive collagen
remodelling. It is the heaviest of the three, with the most downtime, and the
right answer for texture and scarring rather than tone.

## Four questions worth asking any clinic

1. Which device, by name, and who operates it?
2. What is the patch-test protocol for my skin tone?
3. How many sessions, and what happens if I see no change after two?
4. What does the price cover — the session, or the course?

A clinic that answers all four without hesitating is a clinic that has thought
about it. If the answer to the fourth is vague, ask again before you pay.

## The honest part

No laser will fix skin that is being undermined by sun exposure. SPF is not an
upsell attached to the end of a treatment plan — it is the part of the plan
that determines whether the rest of it holds.

7 Questions to Ask Before Booking a Skin Clinic | The Better Face
The questions that separate a clinic from a counter: who treats you, what it really costs, what happens if it goes wrong. Print this and take it with you.

You are allowed to interview a clinic. Most people do not, because the room is
designed to make you feel like the decision has already been made. Here is what
to ask, and what a good answer sounds like.

## 1. Who will actually perform the treatment?

Not who owns the clinic, not who did your consultation. The person holding the
device. Ask for their registration number and their training on that specific
machine. A good clinic answers this in one sentence without checking.

## 2. What device are you using, and why that one?

"A laser" is not an answer. Pigment, vessels, hair and water absorb light
differently, and a device tuned for one is close to useless for another. If the
answer is vague, the treatment plan is too.

## 3. What is the total cost, in writing, today?

Per session and for the whole course. The most common complaint in aesthetics
is not a bad result — it is a bill that grew. Clear, itemised pricing and a
written quote before booking should be the minimum.

## 4. What happens if it does not work?

Ask what the review point is, how many sessions in, and what the clinic does
if you reach it without change. A plan with no review point is not a plan.

## 5. What are the side effects, and what is rare but serious?

Every real treatment has both. A clinic that only lists the mild ones has
either not thought about it or has decided not to tell you.

## 6. Who do I call at 9pm if something goes wrong?

Complications are uncommon and almost all of them resolve quickly when treated
early. The clinics worth trusting have a number and an answer.

## 7. Is there a reason I should not have this?

The most useful question on the list. If a clinic cannot name a single person
they would turn away for this treatment, they are not assessing anyone.

## What a no sounds like

"That will not fix what is bothering you" is the most valuable sentence a
clinician can say to you. It costs them the booking. If you never hear it from
a clinic, that tells you something about how they decide.

Why Pigmentation Returns After Laser | SPF & Aftercare | The Better Face
Pigmentation that returns is usually not treatment failure. It is sun, hormones, or heat. What actually holds a result, and what quietly undoes it.

Someone finishes a course, the skin looks even, and four months later the
patches are back. Almost always, the treatment worked. Something else undid it.

## Pigment cells are not removed, they are quietened

Laser and peels break down pigment that has already been made. They do not
remove the cells that make it. Those cells are still there, still responsive,
and still waiting for a trigger.

## The three triggers

**Ultraviolet light.** The obvious one, and the one people underestimate in a
tropical climate. Incidental exposure — the walk to the car, the drive, the
window seat — adds up to more annual UV than a beach holiday does.

**Hormones.** Melasma in particular is driven by oestrogen and progesterone.
Pregnancy, the combined pill and some hormonal treatments will drive it back
regardless of how good the laser was. This is why we ask.

**Heat.** Less well known and genuinely underrated. Cooking over a stove, hot
yoga, a steam room — infrared and simple heat can provoke melasma without any
UV at all.

## What actually holds a result

SPF 50, broad spectrum, every morning, reapplied if you are outdoors. That is
the whole intervention, and it is the one people skip. Tinted formulations
containing iron oxide do noticeably better against melasma because they block
visible light as well as UV.

Then maintenance: a topical that keeps the cells quiet between courses, and a
single session at the interval your clinician sets rather than waiting for the
patches to come back first.

## What we will tell you at consultation

Melasma is managed, not cured. If your pigmentation is hormonally driven, we
will say so before you spend money, and we will set the expectation as control
rather than clearance. Anyone promising otherwise is selling you something.

Chemical Peel | Brighter, Smoother Skin | The Better Face
A controlled exfoliating peel that lifts dull, damaged surface skin for smoother, brighter tone. Strength matched to your skin at The Better Face.
A controlled exfoliating treatment that removes damaged surface cells to reveal smoother, brighter skin — with the strength matched to you.
Often a short course, 2–4 weeks apart

Active, inflamed acne breakouts — we treat those first
Recent sun exposure or a fresh tan
Pregnancy for certain peel types — flagged at consultation

## What it actually does

A peel uses a controlled solution to loosen and lift the damaged outer layer of
skin, so the fresher skin beneath comes through smoother and brighter. The strength
and type are chosen for your skin and your concern — a peel that suits one face can
be wrong for another.

## What to expect

A short treatment with a warm or tingling feeling, then a few days where the skin
may look flushed and flake lightly as it renews. Depth is matched to how much
downtime you can take and what your skin will tolerate, which is why we assess first
rather than run one standard peel for everyone.

## Aftercare

SPF 50 every morning, no picking at flaking skin, and no actives until we clear you.
New skin is more sun-sensitive, so protecting it is the difference between a bright
result and fresh pigmentation.

CO2 Fractional Laser | Acne Scars & Texture | The Better Face
CO₂ fractional laser resurfacing for acne scars, pores, texture and fine lines, delivered by a qualified clinician. Consultation first at The Better Face.
A resurfacing laser that makes controlled micro-injuries to trigger skin renewal and collagen, softening scars, pores, texture and fine lines.
Redness and flaking for 5–7 days, longer after deeper settings
Uneven texture, fine lines and sun-damaged skin
Skin that has not shifted with gentler resurfacing

## What it actually does

CO₂ fractional laser treats the skin in tiny columns rather than all at once,
leaving healthy tissue in between to speed healing. Those controlled micro-injuries
prompt the skin to rebuild, which is what softens scars and smooths texture over the
weeks that follow.

Because it is a genuine resurfacing laser, it does more than a facial — and it asks
more of you in downtime. We will be clear at consultation about the trade-off before
you book.

## What to expect

Numbing first, then the treatment, then several days of redness and flaking while the
surface renews — longer if we treat deeper. Most of the change appears gradually as
new collagen forms, not on the day. Deeper scarring usually needs more than one
session, and we will give you a realistic number rather than an average.

## Aftercare

SPF 50 every morning while you heal and for months after — sun is what undoes a
resurfacing result. Keep the skin clean and moisturised, skip actives until we say,
and call us if anything looks unexpected.

Platelet-rich plasma from your own blood, used to support skin renewal and hair-restoration programs. Assessed first at The Better Face.
Uses platelet-rich plasma prepared from your own blood to support skin renewal, and to complement scalp and hair-restoration programs.
Usually a short course, spaced weeks apart
Mild redness or bruising for a day or two
Skin that looks tired, or early textural change
As part of a scalp and hair-restoration plan
Anyone who prefers a treatment that uses their own blood
Certain blood conditions or blood-thinning medication — flagged at consultation
Active infection in the treatment area

## What it actually does

We take a small sample of your blood and separate out the platelet-rich plasma —
the fraction rich in the growth factors your body already uses to repair itself.
That plasma is then used across the treatment area to support skin renewal, or as
part of a scalp and hair-restoration plan.

Because it comes from you, there is nothing foreign introduced. It is a support to a
plan rather than a one-off fix, and it works best alongside the rest of your program.

## What to expect

A blood draw, a short preparation, then the treatment. Expect mild redness — and
occasionally light bruising — for a day or two. Results build gradually over a course
rather than appearing after a single session.

## Before we treat

We screen your history at consultation. Some medications and blood conditions make
PRP unsuitable, and we would rather find that out before your appointment than on the
day.

Radio Frequency Skin Tightening | Face & Body | The Better Face
Radio frequency skin tightening and contouring for the face or body, non-invasively, with suitability assessed first. The Better Face.
Non-invasive radio frequency that warms the deeper layers of skin to support tightening and gentle contouring, on the face or body.
Localised areas you would like gently firmed or contoured
Anyone wanting a comfortable treatment with no downtime
Significant laxity or weight-loss goals — this is neither surgery nor slimming
Implants, pacemakers or metal in the treatment area

## What it actually does

Radio frequency delivers controlled heat into the deeper layers of the skin, which
is used to support tightening and improve the appearance of localised areas on the
face or body. It is non-invasive — no surgery, no needles, no downtime, just warm
skin for a little while after.

It works on mild laxity and gentle contouring. It is not a substitute for weight loss
or for surgery, and we will be honest at consultation about which of those your goal
really needs.

## What to expect

A comfortable, warming session, usually delivered as a short course spaced across
weeks. Results build gradually as the tissue responds, rather than appearing after a
single visit.

## Who it suits

Best for someone with a specific area and realistic expectations. We assess the area
first and tell you whether RF is the right tool — or whether Exilis, HIFU or another
approach would serve you better.

Anti-Dandruff Scalp Treatment | Flakes & Itch | The Better Face
A deep-cleansing scalp treatment for dandruff, flaking, itch and buildup, assessed by a clinician first. Book at The Better Face.
A deep-cleansing treatment that clears buildup, oil and flakes and helps soothe an itchy, dry or dandruff-prone scalp.
Often a short course, 1–2 weeks apart
A flaky, itchy or dandruff-prone scalp
Product and oil buildup that shampoo has not cleared
Settling the scalp before starting a regrowth plan
Open wounds, sores or active scalp infection — we treat that first
Scalp psoriasis or eczema that needs medical dermatology
An undiagnosed rash we have not assessed

## What it actually does

A deep-cleansing scalp treatment lifts away the buildup, excess oil, flakes and
product residue that ordinary shampoo leaves behind. Clearing that layer helps calm
an itchy, dry or dandruff-prone scalp and gives whatever you use at home a cleaner
surface to work on.

A healthy scalp is also the foundation of a regrowth plan, which is why we often start
here before anything else.

## What to expect

A thorough cleanse and treatment of the scalp, with no downtime — you can carry on
with your day straight after. Persistent or severe flaking often improves over a
short course rather than a single visit.

## When it is not the answer

Dandruff and a medical scalp condition can look alike. If what we see is psoriasis,
eczema or an infection, we will say so and point you to the right care rather than
sell you a cleanse that will not fix it.

Warts Removal | Per Area | The Better Face
Targeted removal of suitable superficial warts and skin growths by area, with the method matched to the lesion. Assessed first at The Better Face.
Targeted removal of suitable superficial skin growths within a defined area, with the method chosen for the type, size and location.
Often one visit; some lesions need review
A small scab per lesion, healing over several days to two weeks
Common superficial warts and skin tags
Growths a clinician has assessed as suitable to remove
A defined area rather than widespread lesions
Any suspicious or changing lesion — this is referred for medical evaluation first
Widespread or recurrent lesions that need dermatology
Removal on the day without an assessment

## What it actually does

We remove suitable superficial growths within a specified area. The method depends on
the type, size, number and location of the lesions — there is no single technique
that fits every growth, which is why the assessment comes before the removal.

## The assessment matters most

Not everything that looks like a wart is one. A clinician checks each lesion first,
and anything suspicious or uncertain is referred for proper medical evaluation before
we touch it. We will never remove something we should have sent for a second opinion.

## What to expect

A quick, targeted treatment, then a small scab in each spot that heals over one to two
weeks depending on the method. Keep the area clean and dry, do not pick, and let us
know if anything looks inflamed rather than settling.
